chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).
Regarding the urines of animals hitting the clothes, he disliked it. So I said to him, 'Is not their flesh permissible?' He said: 'Yes, but it is not from what Allah made for eating.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal urine touching clothes in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between ritual purity (taharah) and culinary permissibility (halal), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explains that while animal meat is designated for consumption, their urine is not, thus rendering it impure (najis) despite the animal's general halal status. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that bodily excretions, unless specifically designated as food, are inherently impure, a view supported by the majority of Shia scholars. The distinction highlights that 'halal' in the context of food does not automatically extend to all bodily substances, reinforcing the need for ritual cleansing before prayer.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Bukeyr Bin Ayn, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)

regarding the urines of the animals hitting the clothes. So he<sup>asws</sup> disliked it. So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is not their flesh Permissible (to eat)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, but it is not from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Made for the eating’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Urwah from Bukayr ibn ’A‘yan from Zurarah who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam,
about the urine of edible animals that pollutes clothes, expressed dislike. I said, ‘It is from an edible animal.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is true but Allah has not made it for eating.’”
